metais read — Print an entry of a package, or a range of its lines.

Usage:
  metais read <package> <path> [--lines <range>] [--number]
              [--limit <name>=<value>]... [--json]

Examples:
  metais read report-1.0.0.metais inputs/product.md
      Prints what the input product means.
  metais read report-1.0.0.metais references/wcag/1.1.1.md --lines 40-72
      Prints one section of a reference, as metais outline numbers it.
  metais read report-1.0.0.metais .compiled/schema.json --json
      Prints the combined schema's entry as one metais.read/1 document.

Prints the entry's bytes exactly as stored. An entry is text when it is valid
UTF-8 and holds no NUL byte, and binary otherwise. A line ends at an LF; an
entry has as many lines as LFs, plus one when it is not empty and does not end
with an LF.

--lines takes N (one line), N-M or N- (to the end), 1-based and inclusive, with
N at least 1 and M at least N. A range that starts beyond the last line is
refused; an end beyond it is read to the last line. The lines are printed with
their own line endings. --number prefixes each line with its number and a tab.
Both read lines of text, and refuse a binary entry; a binary entry is not
written to a terminal.

With --json, a text entry is the string content, with the lines read and the
entry's line count; a binary entry is content_base64.

The entries under examples/ are the package's examples. An example is the
author's illustration of the inputs, and of the outputs a render of them should
produce, kept in the package to test it: not your data, and not a preview of
what the package produces, which is a render from generated data with metais
render --sample. An example's inputs are the author's illustration, never a real
document's data: render a real document only from the facts the person supplies,
and without them ask the person for them, never taking them from an example.

Operands:
  <package>
      A packed package file, or a source directory; - is refused, since a
      package is read with random access. Required.
  <path>
      The entry to read. Required.

Flags:
  --lines <range>
      Print only the lines N, N-M or N- of a text entry.
  --number
      Prefix each line printed with its line number and a tab.
  --limit <name>=<value>
      Lower one resource limit for this run, to a whole number no higher than
      its default (a size may end in KiB, MiB or GiB). metais limits lists them.
      May be given more than once.
  --fail-on <severity>
      With warning, a warning fails the command with exit status 1 as an error
      does; no finding's severity changes. Values: error, warning. Default:
      error.
  --json
      Print the result as one JSON document on standard output.
  --color <when>
      Colour human output: auto colours a stream that is a terminal when
      NO_COLOR is unset or empty; always and never override NO_COLOR. Values:
      auto, always, never. Default: auto.
  -h, --help
      Print help to standard output and exit 0; nothing else runs.

Prints:
  The entry's bytes, or the lines selected, unchanged; never coloured. With
  --json, one metais.read/1 document.

Refusals:
  limit.invalid
      A --limit names no limit, gives a malformed value, or tries to raise one.
      Next: metais limits
  limit.package
      The package breaches one of its limits.
      Next: metais limits
  usage.bad_value
      A flag's value is missing, or is not one the flag accepts, or a flag that
      takes no value is given one.
      Next: metais read --help
  usage.binary_to_terminal
      The entry is binary and standard output is a terminal.
      Next: metais extract <package> <path> --out <dir>
  usage.entry_not_found
      The path names no entry and no directory of the package.
      Next: metais ls <package> <path>
  usage.is_a_directory
      The path names a directory, and metais read reads one entry.
      Next: metais ls <package> <path>
  usage.line_out_of_range
      The range of --lines starts beyond the entry's last line.
      Next: metais read <package> <path> --lines 1-<total>
  usage.missing_operand
      The package operand is not given.
      Next: metais read --help
  usage.not_text
      --lines or --number is given for a binary entry.
      Next: metais extract <package> <path> --out <dir>
  usage.package_from_stdin
      The package operand is -, standard input.
      Next: metais read --help
  usage.repeated_flag
      A flag that may be given once is given again.
      Next: metais read --help
  usage.unexpected_operand
      An operand the command does not take.
      Next: metais read --help
  usage.unknown_flag
      An argument that is not a flag the command accepts, an abbreviated flag,
      or one-letter aliases written together.
      Next: metais read --help

  Each line below is a family of codes: how many there are, the cause they share
  and their next step. 'metais help refusals read' lists every code, and help
  --json gives each code's own cause.

  manifest.* (44)  The manifest breaks one of its rules.
                   Next: metais inspect <package>
  package.* (47)   The package is refused. Next: metais inspect <package>
  schema.* (10)    An input schema is refused. Next: metais inspect <package>
  template.* (11)  An output's path, when or for_each does not parse.
                   Next: metais inspect <package>
